+# Time-Space Shadow Attribution Design
+
+## Objective
+
+Test whether early reversals after a confirmed structural breakout destroy
+trend value because the system treats price state without sufficient elapsed
+time context. The first version is observation-only and has no authority over
+targets, risk, orders or positions.
+
+## Isolation boundary
+
+Time-space state is an immutable research sidecar keyed by
+`(alpha_id, cutoff_time_ns)`. Stage-specific decision IDs are diagnostic links;
+A1 does not manufacture a `DecisionSnapshot`. The sidecar is not added to
+`DecisionSnapshot`, `TargetPosition`, episode ledger state or the A1-A5 exposure
+formula. Shadow OFF and ON must leave snapshots, targets, orders, fills, equity
+and episodes byte-identical.
+
+```text
+confirmed 4h OHLC + PIT structure indicators + alpha snapshot
+                              |
+                              v
+                    TimeSpaceStateBuilder
+                              |
+                   alpha / approved / filled flips
+                              |
+                              v
+                   TimeSpaceFlipObservation
+                              |
+                   1/2/3/6-bar labels
+                              |
+                              v
+                  research-only attribution
+```
+
+## Point-in-time state
+
+`TimeSpaceState` records:
+
+- `state_id`, `alpha_id`, `cutoff_time_ns` and `decision_id_by_stage`;
+- `feature_available_at_ns`, equal to the confirmed cutoff;
+- formula, config and source-data identities;
+- market structure side;
+- market trend age as both retained 4h bars and elapsed nanoseconds;
+- long and short breakout age as retained bars and elapsed time;
+- UTC week identity and weekly completion fraction;
+- long-side and short-side structure integrity;
+- source gap bars and quality flags;
+- constant `blocks_order=false`.
+
+Market trend age is the age of the current confirmed 4h structure state.
+Breakout age begins when price first crosses a swing boundary visible at the
+previous cutoff. A pivot confirmed by the current bar cannot define a breakout
+on that same bar. The breakout associated with a flip is the old side's most
+recent still-valid same-direction breakout. A later opposite breakout,
+structure reset or source-data gap invalidates the association and produces
+`UNKNOWN`.
+
+The calendar week is the half-open interval `[Monday 00:00 UTC, next Monday
+00:00 UTC)`. A bar is assigned by its covered interval rather than only its
+close timestamp: the bar ending Monday 00:00 closes the prior week at `1.0`;
+the next bar belongs to the new week.
+
+Structure integrity for the old side is:
+
+- `INTACT`: confirmed structure still agrees and its PIT invalidation swing has
+  not been crossed;
+- `BROKEN`: confirmed structure reversed or the invalidation swing was crossed;
+- `UNKNOWN`: missing boundary, neutral structure, source gap or insufficient evidence.
+
+`UNKNOWN` is never treated as `INTACT`.
+
+## Flip populations
+
+- `alpha_flip`: A1_SIGN raw-score sign changes; this is the primary causal population.
+- `approved_flip`: A5 approved target crosses to the opposite side.
+- `filled_flip`: the actual filled position crosses zero; execution diagnostic only.
+
+Flat transitions, same-side reductions and reduce-only safety actions are not
+flips. A partial fill is a `filled_flip` if and only if actual filled position
+sign crosses zero.
+
+## Counterfactual labels
+
+For horizons `1, 2, 3, 6` confirmed 4h bars, record:
+
+```text
+flip_unit_return_h     = new_side * return(cutoff, cutoff+h)
+hold_old_unit_return_h = old_side * return(cutoff, cutoff+h)
+hold_minus_flip_h      = hold_old_unit_return_h - flip_unit_return_h
+```
+
+The primary comparison uses fixed 1x unit direction returns so sizing cannot
+contaminate the directional hypothesis. Actual fees, slippage, approved weight
+and execution outcome remain separate diagnostics. Each label records its own
+availability timestamp; unavailable tail labels are right-censored.
+
+## Pre-registered primary condition
+
+The primary population is defined without searching an hour threshold:
+
+```text
+flip and corresponding breakout occur in the same UTC week
+AND structure_integrity_for_old_side == INTACT
+AND source_gap_bars == 0
+```
+
+Continuous ages and weekly progress remain descriptive variables in V1. Long
+decline and long base are not V1 conditions; adding either is a new hypothesis.
+
+## Evidence roles
+
+- 2025 late-dev: `DISCOVERY_ONLY`; may test code and reproduce motivating events.
+- 2026 data through the exact frozen cutoff: `TEST_REUSED_DIAGNOSTIC`; it has
+  already informed prior testing and cannot become clean OOS evidence.
+- all data available before trusted registration: retrospective falsification
+  only.
+- confirmation begins at the first confirmed 4h cutoff at least 24 hours after
+  an append-only remote-provider or CI receipt. The receipt binds the manifest
+  hash, commit SHA, remote identity and server-side receipt time. Local Git
+  timestamps are not trusted; a missing or unverifiable receipt yields
+  `REGISTRATION_UNVERIFIED`.
+
+An unperturbed canonical path assigns every primary event a stable
+`base_flip_id`. A perturbed seed may map to that event only when old side, new
+side and alpha identity match and its cutoff is within one retained 4h bar;
+otherwise that seed-event is censored. Five perturbation seeds measure path
+stability but are not independent statistical samples.
+
+The Task 5 runner can authenticate the frozen hypothesis/execution receipts,
+but the architecture export itself is not yet a registered derivative of the
+replay corpus. Until Task 6 provides mechanically bound exporter provenance,
+the runner permits that export only for `TEST_REUSED_DIAGNOSTIC`, marks it
+`REUSED_DIAGNOSTIC_ONLY`, and fails closed with
+`EXPORT_REGISTRATION_REQUIRED` for `FORWARD_CONFIRMATION`. Copied formula,
+config, execution, and source hashes are consistency checks, not proof of export
+origin, and can never accrue confirmation evidence.
+
+## Acceptance and rejection
+
+Before forward observation begins, the manifest freezes:
+
+- formula/config/source-set hashes and an exact half-open research window;
+- a separate registration envelope containing the trusted receipt and derived
+  first eligible 4h cutoff, so the manifest never hashes or timestamps itself;
+- `6` bars as the only primary horizon; `1/2/3` are descriptive and cannot
+  promote the hypothesis;
+- arithmetic mean canonical-path `hold_minus_flip_6` as the primary statistic;
+- minimum effect of `15bp` and a one-sided 95% block-bootstrap lower bound above
+  zero, with blocks formed by UTC calendar month;
+- at least `30` unique post-registration primary flips, `180` elapsed days and
+  one confirmed market-state transition;
+- primary gross fixed-1x direction returns; cost-adjusted results are secondary;
+- minimum 4/5 perturbation paths with positive mean `hold_minus_flip_6`;
+- rejection when the sign exists only after selecting favorable age buckets.
+
+Pre-registration history may initialize PIT state, but only flips occurring
+after the registration cutoff and labels maturing afterward enter acceptance.
+`source_gap_bars` counts missing source 4h intervals between planned cutoffs;
+perturbation dropout is recorded separately. When no valid prior breakout
+exists, breakout age is `null` and association quality is `UNKNOWN`, never zero.
+
+V1 can recommend only `continue_observation`, `reject_hypothesis` or
+`eligible_for_separate_activation_review`. It cannot emit a risk multiplier,
+target or order recommendation.
+
+## Verification
+
+- future OHLC changes cannot alter cutoff features;
+- breakout boundaries are visible at `t-1`;
+- bar-count age and elapsed time diverge correctly under dropout;
+- UTC week semantics are timezone and DST independent;
+- flip populations do not collapse into one another;
+- label availability and right-censoring are exact;
+- canonical replay hashes are deterministic;
+- shadow OFF/ON execution material is byte-identical;
+- 2025 can never produce `CONFIRMED` or `PASS`.

+# v164 Eligibility and Forward Validation Design
+
+## Objective
+
+Determine whether v164 contains directionally distinct information worth a
+single forward validation. This is an eligibility study, not a declaration that
+v164 is an independent donor or a request to tune it.
+
+## Existing evidence
+
+v164 was the top train diagnostic from a 12-trial, 152-parameter smoke campaign
+whose formal winner remained `paulwei_baseline`. It was never frozen for
+handoff. Gate v2 later observed:
+
+- late-dev baseline positive on 5/5 seeds;
+- late-dev extra-15bp positive on 4/5 seeds;
+- complete Gate passed on 0/5 seeds;
+- unstable 2021/2022 behavior and train/capacity blockers.
+
+It belongs to the same signal family as August: the indicator configuration and
+signal weights match, while multi-momentum direction-plugin overrides and many
+strategy, risk and execution parameters differ. Independence must be measured
+rather than assumed.
+
+## Identity freeze
+
+`v164_donor_v1` receives an immutable manifest containing:
+
+- exact source result and selector;
+- parameter, profile, formula and source-code hashes;
+- data cutoff and quality manifest;
+- fixed seeds, noise, dropout and costs;
+- explicit train, retrospective, quasi-OOS and forward roles;
+- no tuning knobs.
+
+The existing August manifest and golden artifacts remain unchanged. The A0-A5
+loader must support a declared manifest schema without replacing the August
+default identity.
+
+## Evaluation phases
+
+### Phase 1: retrospective mechanism attribution
+
+Run train and 2025 dev through the same fixed-notional A1 and V2 A2-A5
+contracts. These windows establish episode, execution and cost mechanics only;
+they are not new OOS evidence.
+
+Compare v164 against August using:
+
+- A1 direction-decision disagreement rate;
+- fixed-notional return correlation;
+- overlapping flip and episode timestamps;
+- incremental return after projecting out August fixed-notional returns.
+
+Independent-donor eligibility requires all of the following retrospective
+thresholds on fixed-notional A1 returns and decisions:
+
+- absolute Pearson return correlation with August no greater than `0.75`;
+- direction-decision disagreement at least `20%` on common valid cutoffs;
+- overlapping same-side episode time no greater than `75%` of v164 exposure.
+
+Failure of any threshold classifies v164 as `same_family_sleeve_only`. Positive
+residual return after projecting out August remains a reported diagnostic and
+cannot override these thresholds.
+
+### Phase 2: one-time historical quasi-OOS
+
+The 2026 history predating manifest registration was inspected globally by
+other strategies. It may be evaluated once for v164 under the label
+`QUASI_OOS_ALREADY_OPENED_GLOBALLY`. Results cannot feed back into parameters,
+thresholds, manifests or the forward Gate.
+
+### Phase 3: authoritative forward evidence
+
+Promotion evidence begins only after manifest registration. It accumulates
+confirmed bars and closed episodes without changing the frozen contract.
+
+## Eligibility gates
+
+The v164 protocol intentionally uses a `4/5` economics rule instead of changing
+the frozen August all-seed rule. Safety and purity rules remain all-seed. Final
+eligibility requires at least `180` forward calendar days, `12` closed episodes,
+four non-overlapping 30-day forward windows containing exposure, and both a
+normal state and one confirmed state transition. Until then the result is
+`INSUFFICIENT_SAMPLE`.
+
+The donor must satisfy:
+
+- baseline forward OOS positive on at least 4/5 perturbation seeds;
+- extra-15bp forward OOS positive on at least 4/5 seeds;
+- closed-episode PF after all observed costs at least `1.15` on 4/5 seeds, with
+  no seed below `1.0`;
+- maximum drawdown below `20%` in every seed and declared forward window;
+- more than `2` switches/day blocks; `5` is an absolute ceiling;
+- executor-created exposure, reversal and overshoot all zero;
+- hostile/stress bars are defined by the frozen A3 state; their cumulative loss
+  may not exceed `5%` of initial capital and their segment MDD may not exceed
+  `8%` on any seed; absence of hostile/stress observations is insufficient;
+- OptionsState execution influence zero;
+- no one of the four or more 30-day forward windows contributes more than 50%
+  of positive gross window profit, where the denominator is the sum of positive
+  forward-window profits.
+
+`NO_LOSS_EPISODES` requires at least two closed episodes. Insufficient episode
+or market-state coverage fails closed.
+
+Capital gates such as 10-12% drawdown, PF target 1.25, Calmar, paper-live episode
+count and realized slippage are later promotion requirements, not a reason to
+relax this research Gate.
+
+## Terminal outcomes
+
+- `reject_v164`;
+- `same_family_sleeve_only`;
+- `continue_forward_observation`;
+- `eligible_for_separate_paper_live_review`.
+
+No result authorizes a third tuning round.

+# Trend Participation Two-Layer Design
+
+## Status and product decision
+
+Approved direction as of 2026-08-25. This revision supersedes the original
+`z84` long/short donor design in this file.
+
+Build two isolated BTC research layers:
+
+1. `TimeSpace Shadow` measures whether early flips abandon structurally intact
+   trends. It remains observation-only.
+2. `Trend Participation Donor V1` attempts to earn the persistent BTC trend
+   premium with a slow `LONG | FLAT` core. It uses a confirmed structural
+   breakout for entry, EMA-family breadth plus market structure for holding,
+   and a confirmed structural failure for exit.
+
+The product objective is lexicographic:
+
+```text
+first:  the final candidate has MDD < 30% in every fixed OOS window and perturbation path
+then:   maximize cost-adjusted OOS net profit and CAGR
+then:   prefer stronger worst-window return and persistent-trend capture
+```
+
+An MDD of `15%–25%` is the intended risk-use range. `25%–30%` is allowed. An
+MDD at or above `30%` is a hard rejection. Very low drawdown is not itself a
+success: a path that leaves most of the approved risk budget unused and cannot
+beat the simple trend controls is economically rejected.
+
+EMA is not the strategy. EMA20–100 is a control family and one measure of trend
+integrity. The donor is a structural state machine. The retired August donor is
+not blended into it, and no current risk or execution layer may manufacture a
+directional reversal.
+
+## Evidence motivating the revision
+
+The repaired August donor has no adequate directional edge in 2025 late-dev:
+
+- `A1_SIGN` is negative even before costs;
+- `A1_SCORE` compresses but does not reverse the loss;
+- A5 earns only about `+0.379%` at an average MDD near `1.15%` and becomes
+  negative under an additional 15bp;
+- its risk layer protects capital but does not create a trend return source.
+
+A strict Binance spot daily reconstruction shows why a slow trend donor is the
+right control. With a common EMA100 warmup, `LONG | CASH`, next-session
+execution and 8bp one-way costs, EMA20–100 reproduces the reported historical
+family result: all 81 variants beat the common-start BTC benchmark, with family
+mean return around `+1,967%` versus about `+752%` for buy-and-hold. This history
+is diagnostic, not promotion evidence. The important finding is that the edge
+survives causal execution and broad parameter variation.
+
+On the exact 2025 fixed-capital comparison, the EMA family also has materially
+more gross edge than August, but uses much more drawdown. The design therefore
+does not copy an EMA strategy or blindly add leverage. It creates a new donor,
+then uses the minimum deterministic risk intervention needed to keep every OOS
+path below the approved 30% ceiling.
+
+## Non-goals
+
+- no pure single-EMA strategy and no selection of a best EMA;
+- no August parameter reuse, blending, retraining or alias donor;
+- no direct `LONG -> SHORT` transition in the core donor;
+- no minimum holding-period lock;
+- no use of trend age, weekly progress or OptionsState as V1 trading authority;
+- no parameter search over lookbacks, thresholds, weights or risk caps;
+- no ML, RL, Optuna, learned hazard model or end-to-end black box;
+- no GitHub Pro, branch-protection or remote-receipt requirement for local
+  research evidence;
+- no live activation from a historical or reused result.
+
+## Architecture and authority
+
+```text
+confirmed spot daily rows
+          |
+          +------------------------------+
+          |                              |
+          v                              v
+EMA-family controls              structural donor state
+81 named correlated baselines    55d breakout / 20d failure
+no donor authority               EMA breadth as hold evidence
+          |                              |
+          +---------------+--------------+
+                          v
+             fixed-1x TrendCoreIntent
+                          |
+                          v
+        deterministic risk-budget scalar (after T1 proof)
+                          |
+                          v
+               private research execution
+                          |
+                          v
+        fills / funding / episodes / cost stress
+
+TimeSpace Shadow and OptionsState remain separate observation-only sidecars.
+```
+
+TimeSpace Shadow semantics remain governed by
+`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-23-time-space-shadow-design.md`; this revision
+does not silently change its populations, labels or authority. The common
+local-evidence and no-live-activation boundaries in this document still apply;
+where the older spec requires a remote registration receipt for local research,
+this approved umbrella revision supersedes that requirement.
+
+The core donor owns only `LONG | FLAT` research direction. Risk may cap, reduce
+or flatten it but may not create `SHORT`. Execution may track the approved
+target but may not score the market, add exposure outside the target or reverse
+the position.
+
+A future tactical-short sleeve is a separate donor and a separate approval.
+Its aggregate ex-ante risk allocation may not exceed 25% of the total strategy
+risk budget, and it may act only while the trend core is `FLAT` **and** hard
+safety permits new risk. In addition, filled core position must be zero within
+quantity epsilon and no core order may remain open. Hard safety may reduce
+existing exposure but may never create a tactical short. On a future
+`FLAT -> LONG` core transition, any tactical short must first cancel its entry
+orders, flatten reduce-only, and confirm zero filled position before the core
+may open long. This document defines that interface boundary but does not
+define or implement a short signal. `UNKNOWN` and a safety-flattened exposure
+whose latent core remains `LONG` never authorize the short sleeve.
+
+Strategy, risk, execution, app, infra, ingestors and live adapters must not
+import this research donor. V1 runs through an isolated research adapter.
+Shadow/control OFF and ON parity replays the same frozen real August/production
+event stream through the operational path, once without the sidecars and once
+with them loaded observation-only. It compares snapshots, targets, orders,
+fills, equity and episodes byte-for-byte. Empty streams, empty objects, mocks
+without actual operational decisions, or comparing one object to its own copy
+cannot satisfy this contract.
+
+## Phase 0: repair and freeze the daily source
+
+The raw Binance spot archive currently reconstructs into a continuous UTC
+daily series from `2017-08-17` through `2026-08-23`, with 3,294 unique rows.
+The checked-in conversion path is not authoritative: the no-header CSV reader
+uses `skiprows=1`, drops the first day of monthly files, and produced a stale
+3,045-row parquet ending `2026-03-31`.
+
+Before computing any new donor result:
+
+1. add a failing regression test for no-header Binance CSV conversion;
+2. repair the converter without changing unrelated ingestion semantics;
+3. refresh the raw archive through the latest fully completed UTC daily close,
+   then rebuild the BTCUSDT spot 1d parquet;
+4. require a unique, monotonic, gap-free UTC daily grid and exact OHLC
+   invariants;
+5. freeze the ordered raw-file manifest hash, normalization-code hash,
+   normalized content hash, first/last completed cutoff and row count;
+6. keep any day later than the last fully completed UTC daily close out of the
+   frozen corpus.
+
+Missing, duplicate, conflicting, non-finite or non-positive rows yield
+`INSUFFICIENT_DATA`. Perpetual candles may not proxy spot. Source repair is
+blind data engineering: it may not calculate a donor result or change the
+formula after results are visible.
+
+## Control baselines
+
+Every experiment reports three executable controls on the exact same capital,
+window, perpetual execution prices, funding and cost assumptions:
+
+1. `PERP_LONG_1X`: long BTC perpetual for the complete evaluation window;
+2. `EMA_FAMILY_20_100`: 81 separate `close > EMA_n` long/cash paths for
+   `n = 20..100`, with `adjust=false`, `min_periods=n` and no selected winner;
+3. `BREAKOUT_ONLY_55_20`: the structural entry and exit below without EMA
+   breadth confirmation.
+
+Spot buy-and-hold is reported separately as `SPOT_BUY_AND_HOLD_REFERENCE`. It
+explains the underlying asset drift but is not an executable gate comparator
+because it has neither perpetual fills nor funding.
+
+All executable paths use the same eligibility and initialization rules. Indicators may
+warm on valid point-in-time history before an evaluation window, but PnL starts
+from flat at the first eligible 4h cutoff inside that window. `PERP_LONG_1X`
+enters at that path's first execution event. A full-history path first becomes
+eligible after 100 consecutive valid daily rows. This common start is recorded
+explicitly; no path may gain performance from a hidden earlier start or a
+carried-in position.
+
+`BREAKOUT_ONLY_55_20` is an exact long/flat state machine:
+
+```text
+FLAT -> LONG when close_t > max(high[t-55:t])
+LONG -> FLAT when close_t < min(low[t-20:t])
+```
+
+It has no EMA condition. All three controls are reported at fixed 1x. After T2
+freezes its scalar, the same constant scalar is also applied independently to
+each control so that final-stage economics can be compared at the same ex-ante
+risk scale without using OOS results to resize either side.
+
+The EMA family is summarized by its median, 25th/75th percentiles, complete
+range and all 81 named results. Family members are correlated controls, not 81
+independent statistical samples. No best member may become the donor.
+
+## Trend Participation Donor V1
+
+### Point-in-time daily inputs
+
+For a UTC daily bar `[D, D+1 day)`, every OHLC field is available at
+`D+1 day`. It may first influence the first confirmed 4h decision cutoff
+strictly later than that timestamp. A bar available at 00:00 UTC therefore
+first affects the 04:00 UTC decision, never the 00:00 decision.
+
+At daily index `t`, compute from completed rows only:
+
+```text
+entry_boundary_t = max(high[t-55 : t])     # previous 55 daily bars
+exit_boundary_t  = min(low[t-20 : t])      # previous 20 daily bars
+
+ema_breadth_t = count(close_t > EMA_n_t for n in 20..100) / 81
+ema_majority_t = ema_breadth_t >= 0.50
+```
+
+The `55/20` horizons are the frozen canonical Turtle-style structural control,
+not parameters selected from BTC results. The `0.50` breadth boundary is the
+literal family majority. Changing any horizon, family member or threshold
+creates a new donor ID and requires a new design approval.
+
+At least 100 consecutive completed daily bars are required. A real source gap
+resets warmup. Invalid input produces `UNKNOWN`, whose approved research target
+is flat.
+
+### Mutually exclusive core state machine
+
+The core state is exactly `FLAT | LONG | UNKNOWN`:
+
+```text
+FLAT:
+  if close_t > entry_boundary_t AND ema_majority_t:
+      LONG
+  else:
+      FLAT
+
+LONG:
+  if close_t < exit_boundary_t AND NOT ema_majority_t:
+      FLAT
+  else:
+      LONG
+
+UNKNOWN:
+  target = FLAT
+  after 100 new consecutive valid rows, resume from FLAT
+```
+
+Entry is caused by a confirmed structural breakout, not by EMA alone. Exit
+requires both a structural failure and loss of broad trend support. The two
+conditions provide hysteresis without a time lock. A large price increase,
+overbought reading, incomplete first weekly bar or short-term reversal cannot
+independently exit or reverse the core.
+
+The state machine never emits `SHORT`. A completed `LONG -> FLAT` transition
+must reach flat before any separately approved tactical sleeve could act.
+
+### Diagnostic time-space fields
+
+The donor records, without granting authority:
+
+- days and retained 4h bars since structural entry;
+- breakout age and current UTC-week completion fraction;
+- EMA breadth and its 1/3/7-day changes;
+- distance to entry and exit boundaries;
+- prior visible swing integrity;
+- path efficiency, episode MFE/MAE and drawdown from the favorable close;
+- TimeSpace and OptionsState IDs available at the same cutoff.
+
+These fields explain whether early exits or later structural failures drive
+performance. They may not change V1 entry, exit, size or safety.
+
+## Research stages and risk use
+
+The experiment is sequential and each stage preserves the previous result:
+
+```text
+C0  controls only: PERP_LONG_1X, all EMA family members, breakout-only
+T1  structural donor, fixed initial capital, fixed 1x, no compounding
+T2  T1 plus one deterministic risk-budget scalar
+T3  T2 plus existing hard safety and the fixed 28% research drawdown kill
+```
+
+No A2–A5 regime multiplier, confidence sizing, no-trade band or cost gate may
+enter T1. This answers whether the donor itself makes money.
+
+T2 uses `TRAIN_FULL` evidence only to compute one scalar, then freezes it for
+every non-train window and perturbation path:
+
+```text
+train_stress_mdd = maximum T1 MDD across canonical TRAIN_FULL and its five seed paths
+risk_scalar = min(1.50, (0.85 * 0.30) / train_stress_mdd)
+```
+
+MDD is represented as a positive equity-loss fraction in `[0, 1]`. If
+`train_stress_mdd <= 0`, the result is invalid. The `0.85` factor reserves a 15%
+buffer below the 30% product ceiling; it is not tuned. T2 multiplies the core
+fixed-notional target by this constant scalar. It does not use OOS results,
+current drawdown or a regime label to resize retrospectively.
+
+T3 may cancel, reduce or flatten for existing `KILL`, `UNSAFE`,
+`REDUCE_ONLY` and mechanical cap violations. It cannot add exposure, restore a
+position before the next confirmed 4h decision or change direction. A research
+drawdown kill latches when marked-to-market research equity first reaches 28%
+drawdown from its path high-water mark. It cancels open orders, submits only
+reduce-only flattening orders, and keeps approved exposure at zero for the
+remainder of that evaluation path. It does not mutate the latent core state or
+turn safety-flat exposure into tactical-short eligibility. This fixed latch
+leaves execution room below the 30% absolute acceptance ceiling; a gap through
+30% still fails the path.
+
+Risk-budget utilization is computed per T3 window/path acceptance row. A row is
+`UNDERUSED_RISK_BUDGET` only when its MDD is below 10% and its net CAGR trails
+the same-scalar EMA-family median for that exact window and path. The final
+candidate fails underuse when the canonical `FORWARD_365D` row or at least 4/5
+forward seed rows carry that flag. Historical underuse flags remain diagnostic.
+The remaining bands are also row-local:
+
+- 10%–15% is conservative;
+- 15%–25% is intended;
+- 25%–30% is allowed stress use;
+- at or above 30% is hard rejection.
+
+## Execution and accounting
+
+T1–T3 use fixed initial capital and no compounding for causal attribution. A
+secondary compounded equity curve may be reported but cannot select or promote
+the donor.
+
+`fixed 1x` means one entry notional equal to initial capital. At a
+`FLAT -> LONG` fill, quantity is fixed from that entry's execution price and is
+held unchanged until the core exits; it is not rebalanced every 4h as price
+moves. T2 multiplies that entry quantity by its one frozen scalar. `PERP_LONG_1X`
+uses the same one-time quantity construction, so it does not receive a
+different constant-leverage rebalance assumption.
+
+Equity is marked at every retained perpetual 5m event and at the final event in
+the half-open window. MDD uses the initial equity plus this complete 5m
+marked-to-market series. An open terminal position is not synthetically filled:
+its unrealized PnL is included at the last mark, while the episode remains open
+and is excluded from closed-episode PF. Funding and fees are booked at their
+actual event cutoffs. If equity is non-positive, the path is `RUIN`, MDD is
+`100%`, CAGR is invalid and the path fails. Otherwise:
+
+```text
+net_cagr = (terminal_equity / initial_equity) ** (365.2425 / elapsed_days) - 1
+```
+
+The first execution event is the first retained BTCUSDT perpetual 5m bar open
+strictly after the confirmed 4h decision cutoff. The adapter stores the signal
+cutoff and execution event timestamp separately. It reuses audited fill,
+fee/slippage, funding and episode-accounting primitives in a private research
+namespace; it does not publish production subjects or create production
+`DecisionSnapshot` records.
+
+Each path reports actual realized turnover and reconciles:
+
+```text
+gross_trading_pnl = realized_fill_pnl + terminal_unrealized_pnl
+net_pnl_base = gross_trading_pnl + funding - fees
+net_pnl_15bp = net_pnl_base - realized_turnover_notional * 0.0015
+net_pnl_25bp = net_pnl_base - realized_turnover_notional * 0.0025
+```
+
+Slippage already embedded in actual fill prices is not deducted twice. The
+15bp result is an acceptance input; 25bp is a non-promoting stress diagnostic.
+
+Closed-episode PF uses episode net PnL after fees and funding. Open episodes are
+reported separately and excluded. Its exact boundary rules are:
+
+- no closed episode: `INSUFFICIENT_SAMPLE` and Gate failure;
+- positive episodes and no loss episodes: `NO_LOSS_EPISODES`; pass only with
+  at least two closed episodes;
+- no positive episode: PF is `0`;
+- otherwise: sum of positive episode net PnL divided by the absolute sum of
+  negative episode net PnL.
+
+`switches/day` counts filled-position side transitions attributed to the UTC
+day of the zero-crossing fill. Entry and exit between long and flat are reported
+as turnover actions but are not direction switches; the V1 core therefore must
+have zero long/short switches. For any future sleeve, Gate uses the maximum UTC
+daily count, while the mean remains diagnostic:
+
+- `<=1/day`: no penalty;
+- `(1,2]/day`: soft flag, may enter dev;
+- `>2/day`: normal Gate rejection;
+- `>5/day`: independent absolute rejection.
+
+## Windows, perturbations and evidence roles
+
+Use the repository's authoritative half-open temporal split and seeds
+`42, 123, 456, 789, 1024`:
+
+| Window ID | Exact UTC half-open interval | Warmup | PnL reset | T2 scalar | May reject | May promote |
+| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
+| `TRAIN_FULL` | `[2020-01-01, 2024-01-01)` | PIT pre-start | flat | yes | integrity only | no |
+| `TRAIN_YEAR_2020..2023` | each UTC calendar year inside `TRAIN_FULL` | PIT pre-start | flat per slice | no | no | no |
+| `DEV_2024_REUSED` | `[2024-01-01, 2025-01-01)` | PIT pre-start | flat | no | yes | no |
+| `DISCOVERY_2025` | `[2025-01-01, 2026-01-01)` | PIT pre-start | flat | no | yes | no |
+| `TEST_2026_REUSED` | `[2026-01-01, F)` | PIT pre-start | flat | no | yes | no |
+| `FORWARD_365D` | `[F, F + 365 calendar days)` | PIT pre-start | flat | no | yes | yes |
+
+`F` is the exact first confirmed 4h cutoff strictly after the common frozen
+source cutoff. It is written as nanoseconds into the committed execution
+manifest before any `FORWARD_365D` market event is read. The complete table,
+including resolved timestamps, source coverage and role flags, is hash-bound
+into every result.
+
+No result may pool rows across evidence roles. `TRAIN_FULL` is the only domain allowed to produce
+the T2 scalar. Annual train slices diagnose regime dependence but cannot alter
+it. Dev, discovery, reused test and forward rows may reject the identity but
+may never resize it. Any implementation that calls 2020–2023 OOS, omits 2024,
+or lets a partial 2026 result enter training fails the split contract.
+
+Local evidence identity consists of committed formula/config manifests, Git
+commit SHA, ordered source-file and normalized-content hashes, exact commands,
+environment lockfile hash and immutable result hashes. No GitHub Pro,
+self-hosted runner, branch-protection rule or remote provider receipt is
+required for research, rejection or continued observation.
+
+Local evidence cannot authorize paper/live capital. Any later deployment review
+may define a separate operational trust contract without changing the donor
+formula or relabeling reused history.
+
+The five deterministic perturbation paths reuse
+`zenquant.historical.perturbation.perturb_events` with an execution-manifest
+hash of that module and this exact config:
+
+```text
+seeds = [42, 123, 456, 789, 1024]
+price_noise_pct = 0.001       # independent Gaussian factor per OHLC field
+volume_noise_pct = 0.05       # independent Gaussian factor, floored at zero
+bar_dropout_pct = 0.02        # independent Bernoulli drop
+execution_delay_bars = 0
+spread_noise_bps = 0
+all adversarial modes = disabled
+```
+
+For each seed, a fresh `random.Random(seed)` is applied independently to each
+ordered stream. Spot daily receives price and volume noise but no dropout, so
+an injected robustness path cannot masquerade as a real required-source gap.
+Copied perpetual 4h decision events and 5m execution events receive the complete
+noise and dropout config. Funding events and the canonical month-label set are
+unchanged. OHLC repair is exact: `high = max(noisy_high, noisy_open,
+noisy_close)` and `low = min(noisy_low, noisy_open, noisy_close)`. Streams do
+not share RNG state or synchronized drop masks. Source integrity runs before
+perturbation, and every perturbed row carries its base row ID and seed.
+
+Any change to the kernel hash, stream list, RNG construction, draw order,
+amplitude or repair rule creates a new experiment identity. Perturbations
+measure path stability, not five independent samples.
+
+### Outcome-independent persistent-trend labels
+
+Trend-capture gates use consecutive, non-overlapping UTC calendar months. A
+month is labeled from spot prices alone, without donor positions or PnL:
+
+```text
+sigma84 = standard deviation of the 84 daily log returns visible before month start
+monthly_move = log(last_completed_daily_close / first_completed_daily_open)
+path_efficiency = abs(monthly_move) / sum(abs(daily_log_return_within_month))
+
+persistent = abs(monthly_move) >= sigma84 * sqrt(completed_days)
+             AND path_efficiency >= 0.50
+direction = UP if monthly_move > 0 else DOWN
+```
+
+The daily open and closes used for labeling come from the same frozen spot
+corpus. Donor and `PERP_LONG_1X` PnL on those labeled months use their own
+causal perpetual fills. Labels are computed once from the canonical
+unperturbed spot corpus, frozen by hash, and reused unchanged for all seed
+paths. A month without 84 valid prior returns is `UNLABELED`.
+
+Monthly strategy PnL is the change in 5m marked-to-market perpetual equity
+between the first retained event at or after consecutive UTC month boundaries.
+This slices a multi-month open episode rather than assigning its whole profit
+to the exit month; fills, fees and funding remain assigned at their actual
+event cutoffs. Capture is the ratio of aggregate PnL sums across labeled months,
+never an average of per-month ratios. These labels are evaluation-only and may
+not affect donor state or size.
+
+```text
+up_capture_15 = sum(T3 net_pnl_15bp in persistent-up months)
+                / sum(PERP_LONG_1X gross_pnl in the same months)
+
+t3_down_loss_15 = max(0, -sum(T3 net_pnl_15bp in persistent-down months))
+perp_down_loss_15 = max(0, -sum(PERP_LONG_1X net_pnl_15bp in the same months))
+```
+
+A non-positive uptrend denominator or a zero `perp_down_loss_15` is
+`INSUFFICIENT_SAMPLE` for its respective comparative gate, not an automatic
+pass.
+
+There is exactly one forward look for this experiment, at `F + 365 calendar
+days`. Sufficient future evidence at that precommitted endpoint means at least
+five closed canonical core episodes and at least one persistent-up and one
+persistent-down month. A path with fewer than two closed episodes is
+`INSUFFICIENT_SAMPLE` for episode PF. If any aggregate sufficiency condition is
+missing at the fixed endpoint, the result is `INSUFFICIENT_FORWARD_SAMPLE` and
+cannot promote. The endpoint may not slide until the first profitable or
+sufficient observation. Any extension requires a separately approved
+prospective evidence envelope frozen before reading events after the old
+endpoint.
+
+## Profit-first gates
+
+Historical and reused evidence can only reject or continue observation. A donor
+may reach `ELIGIBLE_FOR_SEPARATE_ACTIVATION_REVIEW` only with sufficient future
+evidence and all of the following. Unless a stage is named explicitly, gates
+apply to the final T3 candidate. `canonical` means the unperturbed path inside
+one evidence role; seed-path results are never pooled with it. Historical role
+metrics are compared as role-level values, while forward gates use only
+`FORWARD_365D` rows. Historical profit may never offset a forward loss.
+
+Every acceptance row records `stage_id`, `path_id` (`canonical` or seed),
+`window_id`, evidence role, metric name, reducer, numerator, denominator,
+threshold, sample count, insufficient-sample policy, result and input hashes.
+The final verdict is a pure reduction over these rows; report code may not infer
+a missing scope or substitute an aggregate.
+
+### Hard safety and integrity
+
+- T3 MDD is strictly below 30% in every fixed non-train window, on the
+  canonical path and all five seed paths;
+- executor-created exposure, unexpected reversal and target overshoot are zero;
+- source, accounting, episode and parity checks reconcile exactly;
+- normal and absolute switch ceilings pass;
+- T3 never creates `SHORT` core exposure.
+
+### Hard economics
+
+- In every non-train historical role containing at least 180 elapsed days, T1
+  fixed-1x `net_pnl_15bp` is positive canonically and in at least 4/5 seed
+  paths. A shorter role is `INSUFFICIENT_SAMPLE`, not a pass.
+- Across those historical roles, the median of T1 fixed-1x role-level
+  `net_cagr_15bp` is not below the median of the corresponding fixed-1x
+  EMA-family medians.
+- In every sufficiently sampled historical role, T1 fixed-1x
+  `net_cagr_15bp` is not below `BREAKOUT_ONLY_55_20` fixed-1x.
+- On `FORWARD_365D` alone, T1 fixed-1x `net_pnl_15bp` is positive
+  canonically and in at least 4/5 seed paths.
+- On `FORWARD_365D` alone, T1 fixed-1x `net_cagr_15bp` is not below
+  `BREAKOUT_ONLY_55_20` fixed-1x on the canonical path and at least 4/5 seed
+  paths.
+- On `FORWARD_365D` alone, T3 `net_pnl_15bp` is positive canonically and in at
+  least 4/5 seed paths. `RUIN` and `INSUFFICIENT_SAMPLE` are failures.
+- On `FORWARD_365D` alone, T3 `net_cagr_15bp` is not below the median
+  EMA-family member after every member receives the same frozen T2 scalar, on
+  the canonical path and at least 4/5 seed paths.
+- On `FORWARD_365D` alone, T3 `net_cagr_15bp` is not below
+  `BREAKOUT_ONLY_55_20` after the control receives the same frozen T2 scalar,
+  on the canonical path and at least 4/5 seed paths.
+- On `FORWARD_365D` alone, T3 persistent-uptrend net capture is at
+  least 70% of `PERP_LONG_1X` gross profit on the same labeled months.
+- On `FORWARD_365D` alone, T3 persistent-downtrend loss is smaller than
+  `PERP_LONG_1X` loss.
+- T3 closed-episode PF is at least 1.0 on every sufficiently sampled forward
+  path.
+
+Calendar-year and episode PnL concentration are reported as diagnostics, not
+hard gates: a one-year forward sample cannot satisfy an honest multi-year
+concentration test.
+
+### Overlay retention
+
+- T2 must reconcile exactly to T1 direction and the frozen risk scalar; every
+  T3 deviation must be exposure-reducing and attributed to a named hard-safety
+  event;
+- For every non-train window/path row with positive T2 `net_pnl_15bp`, T3 must
+  retain at least 80% of that row's T2 `net_pnl_15bp`. The exception applies
+  only when that same T2 row has MDD at or above 30%; it never spills into
+  another row and never waives T3 forward-profit or MDD gates.
+- A candidate meeting the forward `UNDERUSED_RISK_BUDGET` failure reducer is
+  rejected even if its Sharpe or MDD improves.
+
+When roles differ in length, historical comparison uses annualized net CAGR.
+The primary forward comparison is full-forward net CAGR after 15bp; tie-breakers
+are worst historical role return, persistent-trend capture and lower turnover,
+in that order. Sharpe and raw hit rate are diagnostics, not primary objectives.
+
+## Rejection conditions
+
+Reject this donor identity rather than tune it when:
+
+- T1 fixed-1x economics are negative after 15bp;
+- edge exists only after selecting an EMA, year, seed, regime or age bucket;
+- entry works only with same-close execution or another lookahead assumption;
+- profit requires breaching 30% MDD in any fixed non-train path;
+- T2/T3 destroys trend profit merely to improve Sharpe or produce very low MDD;
+- the donor cannot match the EMA-family median after risk and cost matching;
+- EMA breadth cannot match the breakout-only control at the required stages;
+- missing spot data requires perpetual or carried-value fallback;
+- any changed horizon, threshold, authority field or exit is presented under
+  the same donor ID.
+
+## Artifacts
+
+Research artifacts are deterministic and local:
+
+- `trend_participation_source_manifest.json`;
+- `trend_participation_formula_manifest.json`;
+- `trend_participation_controls.json`;
+- `trend_participation_stage_attribution.json`;
+- `trend_participation_episode_ledger.json`;
+- `trend_participation_acceptance.json`;
+- one canonical Markdown summary generated from the JSON authority.
+
+The JSON artifacts are authoritative. Documentation may summarize but may not
+change a result or evidence role.
+
+## Verification
+
+- converter regression proves no first row is dropped from no-header CSV;
+- reconstructed daily data has an exact gap-free UTC grid and stable hashes;
+- future daily rows cannot alter earlier donor state;
+- daily availability and first eligible 4h decision are exact;
+- entry boundaries use only prior 55 bars and exit boundaries only prior 20;
+- EMA breadth includes exactly EMA20–100 with no selected winner;
+- state transitions are mutually exclusive and never emit short;
+- source gaps reset the complete 100-row warmup;
+- T1 has no hidden sizing, regime or execution authority;
+- fixed-1x quantity remains constant inside each long episode;
+- the resolved window table proves only `TRAIN_FULL` can produce the scalar;
+- risk scalar uses train paths only and remains byte-identical across non-train
+  runs;
+- hard safety can only reduce absolute exposure;
+- the 28% drawdown kill latches for the complete evaluation path;
+- fill, fee, funding, turnover and episode PnL reconcile;
+- terminal open-position MTM, 5m MDD and CAGR boundary cases are golden-tested;
+- monthly MTM attribution reconciles to total equity and seed paths reuse the
+  canonical label set;
+- 15bp/25bp cost stress does not double-count embedded slippage;
+- evidence roles cannot relabel 2025 or reused 2026 as forward;
+- the forward endpoint is fixed before observation and cannot slide;
+- OFF/ON parity uses the same non-empty frozen operational replay stream;
+- research imports cannot flow into operational modules;
+- complete focused tests and `zenquant-check` run before merge.
+
+## References
+
+- Moskowitz, Ooi and Pedersen, *Time Series Momentum*.
+- Kim, Tse and Wald, *Time Series Momentum and Volatility Scaling*.
+- Richard Donchian's channel breakout and the canonical Turtle `55/20`
+  long-term system.
+- Kang and Ryu (2026), Bitcoin trend-following speed comparison.
+- Sepp and Lucic, `TrendFollowingSystems` replication repository.

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Publish a frozen late-development cost diagnosis from an explicit JSON input."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import argparse
+import hashlib
+import json
+import sys
+from pathlib import Path
+from typing import Any
+
+sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).parent.parent))
+
+from zenquant.research.late_dev_cost_attribution import (
+    LateDevAttributionValidationError,
+    build_late_dev_cost_attribution,
+    build_late_dev_cost_attribution_markdown,
+    build_regime_objective_hypothesis,
+    canonical_late_dev_attribution_bytes,
+)
+
+_HASH_CHUNK_BYTES = 1024 * 1024
+_REPORT_FILENAME = "late_dev_cost_attribution.json"
+_MARKDOWN_FILENAME = "late_dev_cost_attribution.md"
+_HYPOTHESIS_FILENAME = "regime_objective_redesign_from_late_dev.json"
+
+
+def _parse_args() -> argparse.Namespace:
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Publish frozen Quant V2 late-development cost attribution")
+    parser.add_argument(
+        "--input",
+        type=Path,
+        default=Path("results/quant_v2_acceptance/architecture_attribution.json"),
+    )
+    parser.add_argument(
+        "--output-dir",
+        type=Path,
+        default=Path("results/quant_v2_late_dev_cost_attribution"),
+    )
+    return parser.parse_args()
+
+
+def _read_input(path: Path) -> tuple[dict[str, Any], str, int]:
+    source_bytes = path.read_bytes()
+    digest = hashlib.sha256()
+    for offset in range(0, len(source_bytes), _HASH_CHUNK_BYTES):
+        digest.update(source_bytes[offset : offset + _HASH_CHUNK_BYTES])
+    payload = json.loads(source_bytes.decode("utf-8"), parse_constant=_reject_nonfinite_json_constant)
+    if not isinstance(payload, dict):
+        raise LateDevAttributionValidationError("raw report must be a JSON object")
+    return payload, digest.hexdigest(), len(source_bytes)
+
+
+def _reject_nonfinite_json_constant(value: str) -> None:
+    raise LateDevAttributionValidationError(f"raw report contains forbidden JSON constant: {value}")
+
+
+def _canonical_json_bytes(payload: Any) -> bytes:
+    return json.dumps(payload, allow_nan=False, indent=2, sort_keys=True).encode("utf-8")
+
+
+def _publish_atomically(output_dir: Path, files: dict[str, bytes]) -> None:
+    output_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+    targets = [output_dir / filename for filename in files]
+    hypothesis_target = output_dir / _HYPOTHESIS_FILENAME
+    if hypothesis_target not in targets:
+        targets.append(hypothesis_target)
+    snapshots = {target: target.read_bytes() if target.exists() else None for target in targets}
+    temporary_paths: list[Path] = []
+    changed_targets: list[Path] = []
+    try:
+        for filename, content in files.items():
+            target = output_dir / filename
+            temporary = target.with_suffix(target.suffix + ".tmp")
+            temporary_paths.append(temporary)
+            temporary.write_bytes(content)
+        for temporary in temporary_paths:
+            target = temporary.with_suffix("")
+            temporary.replace(target)
+            changed_targets.append(target)
+        if _HYPOTHESIS_FILENAME not in files:
+            changed_targets.append(hypothesis_target)
+            hypothesis_target.unlink(missing_ok=True)
+    except OSError:
+        _restore_publication(changed_targets, snapshots)
+        raise
+    finally:
+        for temporary in temporary_paths:
+            temporary.unlink(missing_ok=True)
+
+
+def _restore_publication(changed_targets: list[Path], snapshots: dict[Path, bytes | None]) -> None:
+    rollback_paths: list[Path] = []
+    try:
+        for target in reversed(changed_targets):
+            previous = snapshots[target]
+            if previous is None:
+                target.unlink(missing_ok=True)
+                continue
+            rollback = target.with_suffix(target.suffix + ".rollback.tmp")
+            rollback_paths.append(rollback)
+            rollback.write_bytes(previous)
+            rollback.replace(target)
+    finally:
+        for rollback in rollback_paths:
+            rollback.unlink(missing_ok=True)
+
+
+def main() -> int:
+    args = _parse_args()
+    try:
+        raw_report, source_sha256, source_size_bytes = _read_input(args.input)
+        attribution = build_late_dev_cost_attribution(
+            raw_report,
+            source_artifact=str(args.input),
+            source_sha256=source_sha256,
+            source_size_bytes=source_size_bytes,
+        )
+        report_bytes = canonical_late_dev_attribution_bytes(attribution)
+        markdown_bytes = build_late_dev_cost_attribution_markdown(attribution).encode("utf-8")
+        hypothesis = build_regime_objective_hypothesis(attribution)
+        files = {
+            _REPORT_FILENAME: report_bytes,
+            _MARKDOWN_FILENAME: markdown_bytes,
+        }
+        if hypothesis is not None:
+            files[_HYPOTHESIS_FILENAME] = _canonical_json_bytes(hypothesis)
+    except (OSError, UnicodeDecodeError, json.JSONDecodeError, LateDevAttributionValidationError) as exc:
+        print(f"invalid input: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
+        return 2
+
+    try:
+        _publish_atomically(args.output_dir, files)
+    except OSError as exc:
+        print(f"output error: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
+        return 2
+
+    recommendation = attribution["terminal_recommendation"]
+    print(json.dumps({"output_dir": str(args.output_dir), "terminal_recommendation": recommendation}, sort_keys=True))
+    return 1 if attribution["evidence"]["required_inputs_incomplete"] is True else 0
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    raise SystemExit(main())

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Write an immutable sidecar describing legacy accounting evidence validity."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import argparse
+import hashlib
+import json
+import os
+import sys
+import tempfile
+from pathlib import Path
+from typing import Any
+
+sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).parent.parent))
+
+from zenquant.research.legacy_accounting_validity import (
+    DEFAULT_ACCOUNTING_VALIDITY_REGISTRY,
+    AccountingValidityRegistryError,
+    load_accounting_validity_registry,
+)
+
+ACCOUNTING_AUDIT_SCHEMA_VERSION = "legacy-accounting-audit.v1"
+_HASH_CHUNK_BYTES = 1024 * 1024
+
+
+def build_parser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser:
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
+    parser.add_argument("--source", required=True, type=Path)
+    parser.add_argument("--registry", type=Path, default=DEFAULT_ACCOUNTING_VALIDITY_REGISTRY)
+    parser.add_argument("--output", required=True, type=Path)
+    return parser
+
+
+def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
+    args = build_parser().parse_args(argv)
+    try:
+        if args.source.resolve() == args.output.resolve():
+            raise AccountingValidityRegistryError("output must not replace the source artifact")
+        registry = load_accounting_validity_registry(args.registry)
+        source_sha256, source_size_bytes = _source_identity(args.source)
+        path_records = registry.records_for_artifact(str(args.source))
+        if path_records and source_sha256 not in {record.source_sha256 for record in path_records}:
+            raise AccountingValidityRegistryError(
+                f"source_sha256_mismatch:{args.source}:"
+                f"expected={sorted({record.source_sha256 for record in path_records})}:actual={source_sha256}"
+            )
+        records = tuple(dict.fromkeys((*path_records, *registry.records_for_sha256(source_sha256))))
+        if not records:
+            raise AccountingValidityRegistryError(f"source has no accounting validity classification:{args.source}")
+        sidecar = {
+            "schema_version": ACCOUNTING_AUDIT_SCHEMA_VERSION,
+            "source": {
+                "artifact_path": str(args.source),
+                "sha256": source_sha256,
+                "size_bytes": source_size_bytes,
+            },
+            "registry": {
+                "path": str(args.registry),
+                "schema_version": registry.schema_version,
+            },
+            "records": [record.to_dict() for record in records],
+        }
+        encoded = _canonical_json_bytes(sidecar)
+        _write_atomically(args.output, encoded, protected_source=args.source)
+    except (AccountingValidityRegistryError, OSError) as exc:
+        print(f"invalid input: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
+        return 2
+    print(json.dumps({"output": str(args.output), "source_sha256": source_sha256}, sort_keys=True))
+    return 0
+
+
+def _source_identity(path: Path) -> tuple[str, int]:
+    digest = hashlib.sha256()
+    size_bytes = 0
+    with path.open("rb") as source:
+        for chunk in iter(lambda: source.read(_HASH_CHUNK_BYTES), b""):
+            digest.update(chunk)
+            size_bytes += len(chunk)
+    return digest.hexdigest(), size_bytes
+
+
+def _canonical_json_bytes(payload: Any) -> bytes:
+    return json.dumps(payload, allow_nan=False, indent=2, sort_keys=True).encode("utf-8")
+
+
+def _write_atomically(path: Path, content: bytes, *, protected_source: Path) -> None:
+    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+    temporary: Path | None = None
+    try:
+        with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(
+            mode="wb",
+            dir=path.parent,
+            prefix=f".{path.name}.",
+            suffix=".tmp",
+            delete=False,
+        ) as output:
+            temporary = Path(output.name)
+            if temporary.resolve() == protected_source.resolve():
+                raise AccountingValidityRegistryError("temporary output must not alias the source artifact")
+            output.write(content)
+            output.flush()
+            os.fsync(output.fileno())
+        os.replace(temporary, path)
+    finally:
+        if temporary is not None:
+            temporary.unlink(missing_ok=True)
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    raise SystemExit(main())

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Build and verify the independent TimeSpace export checkpoint receipt."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import argparse
+import hashlib
+import json
+from collections.abc import Mapping, Sequence
+from datetime import UTC, datetime
+from pathlib import Path
+from typing import Any
+
+ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
+MANIFEST_ROOT = "config/research/registrations/time_space_exports"
+TRUST_PATH = ROOT / "config/research/time_space_export_registration_trust_v1.json"
+WORKFLOW_PATH = ".github/workflows/time-space-export-checkpoint.yml"
+BRANCH = "feature/trend-registration-time-space-export"
+REPOSITORY = "infdahai/zenQuant"
+MANIFEST_KEYS = {
+    "schema_version",
+    "layer",
+    "registration_status",
+    "export_sha256",
+    "provenance_sha256",
+    "receipt",
+    "as_of_ns",
+    "generator_provider_run_id",
+    "source_slice_sha256",
+}
+
+
+def build_receipt(
+    *,
+    manifest_path: str,
+    manifest_bytes: bytes,
+    provider: Mapping[str, Any],
+    artifact: Mapping[str, Any],
+    generator_export_bytes: bytes,
+    generator_provenance_bytes: bytes,
+    generator_artifact: Mapping[str, Any],
+) -> dict[str, Any]:
+    """Build a receipt using only the checked-in trust root."""
+
+    return _build_receipt(
+        manifest_path=manifest_path,
+        manifest_bytes=manifest_bytes,
+        provider=provider,
+        artifact=artifact,
+        generator_export_bytes=generator_export_bytes,
+        generator_provenance_bytes=generator_provenance_bytes,
+        generator_artifact=generator_artifact,
+        trust=_load_json(TRUST_PATH),
+    )
+
+
+def _build_receipt(
+    *,
+    manifest_path: str,
+    manifest_bytes: bytes,
+    provider: Mapping[str, Any],
+    artifact: Mapping[str, Any],
+    generator_export_bytes: bytes,
+    generator_provenance_bytes: bytes,
+    generator_artifact: Mapping[str, Any],
+    trust: Mapping[str, Any],
+) -> dict[str, Any]:
+    manifest = _validate_manifest(manifest_path, manifest_bytes)
+    as_of_ns = _manifest_as_of(manifest_path)
+    expected_workflow_id = trust.get("checkpoint_workflow_id")
+    if isinstance(expected_workflow_id, bool) or not isinstance(expected_workflow_id, int) or expected_workflow_id <= 0:
+        raise ValueError("checkpoint workflow id is not independently pinned")
+    expected = {
+        "id": provider.get("id"),
+        "head_sha": provider.get("head_sha"),
+        "created_at": provider.get("created_at"),
+        "conclusion": provider.get("conclusion"),
+        "event": provider.get("event"),
+        "head_branch": provider.get("head_branch"),
+        "path": provider.get("path"),
+        "workflow_id": provider.get("workflow_id"),
+        "repository": provider.get("repository"),
+    }
+    if expected["conclusion"] != "success" or expected["event"] != "push":
+        raise ValueError("provider checkpoint did not complete a successful push")
+    if expected["head_branch"] != BRANCH or expected["path"] != WORKFLOW_PATH:
+        raise ValueError("provider checkpoint branch or workflow path changed")
+    if expected["workflow_id"] != expected_workflow_id:
+        raise ValueError("provider checkpoint workflow id changed")
+    repository = expected["repository"]
+    if not isinstance(repository, Mapping) or repository.get("full_name") != REPOSITORY:
+        raise ValueError("provider checkpoint repository changed")
+    run_id = expected["id"]
+    if isinstance(run_id, bool) or not isinstance(run_id, int) or run_id <= 0:
+        raise ValueError("provider run id is invalid")
+    head_sha = _sha(expected["head_sha"], 40, "provider head sha")
+    created_at_ns = _timestamp_ns(expected["created_at"])
+    expected_artifact_name = f"time-space-export-checkpoint-{as_of_ns}-{run_id}"
+    generator_export = _canonical_payload(generator_export_bytes, "generator export")
+    generator_provenance = _canonical_payload(generator_provenance_bytes, "generator provenance")
+    if (
+        _canonical_sha256(generator_export) != manifest["export_sha256"]
+        or _canonical_sha256(generator_provenance) != manifest["provenance_sha256"]
+        or generator_export.get("as_of_ns") != as_of_ns
+        or generator_provenance.get("as_of_ns") != as_of_ns
+        or _canonical_sha256(generator_provenance.get("source_files")) != manifest["source_slice_sha256"]
+    ):
+        raise ValueError("downloaded generator artifact content does not match checkpoint")
+    generator_run_id = int(manifest["generator_provider_run_id"])
+    expected_generator_name = f"time-space-export-{as_of_ns}-{generator_run_id}"
+    if (
+        generator_artifact.get("name") != expected_generator_name
+        or generator_artifact.get("expired") is not False
+        or isinstance(generator_artifact.get("id"), bool)
+        or not isinstance(generator_artifact.get("id"), int)
+        or generator_artifact["id"] <= 0
+    ):
+        raise ValueError("generator artifact identity is invalid")
+    workflow_run = artifact.get("workflow_run")
+    if (
+        artifact.get("expired") is not False
+        or artifact.get("name") != expected_artifact_name
+        or isinstance(artifact.get("id"), bool)
+        or not isinstance(artifact.get("id"), int)
+        or not isinstance(workflow_run, Mapping)
+        or workflow_run.get("id") != run_id
+        or workflow_run.get("head_sha") != head_sha
+    ):
+        raise ValueError("checkpoint artifact identity changed")
+    return {
+        "schema_version": "time-space-export-registration-receipt.v1",
+        "manifest_path": manifest_path,
+        "manifest_sha256": hashlib.sha256(manifest_bytes).hexdigest(),
+        "export_sha256": manifest["export_sha256"],
+        "provenance_sha256": manifest["provenance_sha256"],
+        "provider_run_id": str(run_id),
+        "provider_created_at_ns": created_at_ns,
+        "commit_sha": head_sha,
+        "remote_identity": REPOSITORY,
+        "workflow": {"id": expected_workflow_id, "path": WORKFLOW_PATH},
+        "event": "push",
+        "ref": f"refs/heads/{BRANCH}",
+        "artifact": {"id": artifact["id"], "name": expected_artifact_name},
+        "generator_artifact": {
+            "id": generator_artifact["id"],
+            "name": expected_generator_name,
+            "export_sha256": manifest["export_sha256"],
+            "provenance_sha256": manifest["provenance_sha256"],
+            "source_slice_sha256": manifest["source_slice_sha256"],
+        },
+    }
+
+
+def _validate_manifest(path: str, content: bytes) -> dict[str, Any]:
+    _manifest_as_of(path)
+    try:
+        manifest = json.loads(content.decode("utf-8"))
+    except (UnicodeError, json.JSONDecodeError) as exc:
+        raise ValueError("checkpoint manifest is not JSON") from exc
+    if not isinstance(manifest, dict) or set(manifest) != MANIFEST_KEYS:
+        raise ValueError("checkpoint manifest schema changed")
+    canonical = (json.dumps(manifest, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":")) + "\n").encode()
+    if content != canonical:
+        raise ValueError("checkpoint manifest bytes are not canonical")
+    if (
+        manifest.get("schema_version") != "time-space-export-checkpoint.v1"
+        or manifest.get("layer") != "time_space_shadow"
+        or manifest.get("registration_status") != "PENDING"
+        or manifest.get("receipt") is not None
+    ):
+        raise ValueError("checkpoint manifest must remain the pending exporter output")
+    _sha(manifest.get("export_sha256"), 64, "export sha")
+    _sha(manifest.get("provenance_sha256"), 64, "provenance sha")
+    _sha(manifest.get("source_slice_sha256"), 64, "source slice sha")
+    if manifest.get("as_of_ns") != _manifest_as_of(path):
+        raise ValueError("checkpoint manifest cutoff does not match path")
+    if (
+        not isinstance(manifest.get("generator_provider_run_id"), str)
+        or not manifest["generator_provider_run_id"].isdigit()
+    ):
+        raise ValueError("checkpoint generator provider run id is invalid")
+    return manifest
+
+
+def _canonical_payload(content: bytes, label: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
+    try:
+        payload = json.loads(content.decode("utf-8"))
+    except (UnicodeError, json.JSONDecodeError) as exc:
+        raise ValueError(f"{label} is not JSON") from exc
+    if not isinstance(payload, dict):
+        raise ValueError(f"{label} must be an object")
+    canonical = (json.dumps(payload, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":")) + "\n").encode()
+    if content != canonical:
+        raise ValueError(f"{label} bytes are not canonical")
+    return payload
+
+
+def _canonical_sha256(value: Any) -> str:
+    encoded = json.dumps(value, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":")).encode()
+    return hashlib.sha256(encoded).hexdigest()
+
+
+def _manifest_as_of(path: str) -> int:
+    prefix = f"{MANIFEST_ROOT}/"
+    suffix = "/time_space_shadow_export_checkpoint_v1.json"
+    if not path.startswith(prefix) or not path.endswith(suffix):
+        raise ValueError("checkpoint manifest path changed")
+    value = path[len(prefix) : -len(suffix)]
+    if not value.isdigit() or value.startswith("0"):
+        raise ValueError("checkpoint manifest path cutoff is invalid")
+    as_of_ns = int(value)
+    if as_of_ns % (4 * 60 * 60 * 1_000_000_000):
+        raise ValueError("checkpoint manifest cutoff is not on the 4h grid")
+    return as_of_ns
+
+
+def _sha(value: Any, length: int, name: str) -> str:
+    if not isinstance(value, str) or len(value) != length or any(c not in "0123456789abcdef" for c in value):
+        raise ValueError(f"{name} is invalid")
+    return value
+
+
+def _timestamp_ns(value: Any) -> int:
+    if not isinstance(value, str):
+        raise ValueError("provider created_at is invalid")
+    try:
+        parsed = datetime.strptime(value, "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ").replace(tzinfo=UTC)
+    except ValueError as exc:
+        raise ValueError("provider created_at is invalid") from exc
+    return int(parsed.timestamp()) * 1_000_000_000
+
+
+def _load_json(path: Path) -> dict[str, Any]:
+    try:
+        payload = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
+    except (OSError, UnicodeError, json.JSONDecodeError) as exc:
+        raise ValueError(f"cannot load JSON: {path}") from exc
+    if not isinstance(payload, dict):
+        raise ValueError(f"JSON payload must be an object: {path}")
+    return payload
+
+
+def _main(argv: Sequence[str] | None = None) -> int:
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
+    parser.add_argument("--manifest", type=Path, required=True)
+    parser.add_argument("--manifest-path", required=True)
+    parser.add_argument("--provider-run-json", type=Path, required=True)
+    parser.add_argument("--artifact-json", type=Path, required=True)
+    parser.add_argument("--generator-export", type=Path, required=True)
+    parser.add_argument("--generator-provenance", type=Path, required=True)
+    parser.add_argument("--generator-artifact-json", type=Path, required=True)
+    parser.add_argument("--output", type=Path, required=True)
+    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
+    receipt = build_receipt(
+        manifest_path=args.manifest_path,
+        manifest_bytes=args.manifest.read_bytes(),
+        provider=_load_json(args.provider_run_json),
+        artifact=_load_json(args.artifact_json),
+        generator_export_bytes=args.generator_export.read_bytes(),
+        generator_provenance_bytes=args.generator_provenance.read_bytes(),
+        generator_artifact=_load_json(args.generator_artifact_json),
+    )
+    args.output.write_text(json.dumps(receipt, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":")) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
+    return 0
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    raise SystemExit(_main())

+"""Dependency-free CLI for trusted trend-research registration receipts."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import argparse
+import importlib.util
+import json
+import sys
+from collections.abc import Sequence
+from pathlib import Path
+from typing import Any
+
+
+def _load_registration_contracts() -> Any:
+    """Load the stdlib-only registration module without importing its package."""
+
+    module_name = "_trend_registration_contracts"
+    module_path = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / "zenquant/research/registration.py"
+    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(module_name, module_path)
+    if spec is None or spec.loader is None:
+        raise RuntimeError(f"cannot load registration contracts: {module_path}")
+    module = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
+    sys.modules[module_name] = module
+    try:
+        spec.loader.exec_module(module)
+    except Exception:
+        del sys.modules[module_name]
+        raise
+    return module
+
+
+_CONTRACTS = _load_registration_contracts()
+RegistrationError = _CONTRACTS.RegistrationError
+
+
+def _load_provider_run(path: Path) -> dict[str, Any]:
+    try:
+        payload = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
+    except (OSError, UnicodeError, json.JSONDecodeError) as exc:
+        raise RegistrationError(f"cannot load provider run payload: {path}") from exc
+    if not isinstance(payload, dict):
+        raise RegistrationError("provider run payload must be a JSON object")
+    return payload
+
+
+def _write_selection(github_env: Path, selection: tuple[str, str]) -> None:
+    manifest_kind, manifest_path = selection
+    with github_env.open("a", encoding="utf-8") as output:
+        output.write(f"MANIFEST_KIND={manifest_kind}\nMANIFEST_PATH={manifest_path}\n")
+
+
+def _build_command(parser: argparse.ArgumentParser) -> None:
+    parser.add_argument("--manifest-path", type=Path, required=True)
+    parser.add_argument("--commit-sha", required=True)
+    parser.add_argument("--provider-run-json", type=Path, required=True)
+    parser.add_argument("--output", type=Path, required=True)
+
+
+def _selection_arguments(parser: argparse.ArgumentParser) -> None:
+    parser.add_argument("--manifest-kind", required=True)
+    parser.add_argument("--manifest-path", required=True)
+    parser.add_argument("--github-env", type=Path, required=True)
+
+
+def main(argv: Sequence[str] | None = None) -> int:
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
+    commands = parser.add_subparsers(dest="command", required=True)
+    build = commands.add_parser("build")
+    _build_command(build)
+    bootstrap = commands.add_parser("select-bootstrap")
+    bootstrap.add_argument("--branch-name", required=True)
+    bootstrap.add_argument("--github-env", type=Path, required=True)
+    manual = commands.add_parser("select-manual")
+    manual.add_argument("--github-ref", required=True)
+    _selection_arguments(manual)
+    validate = commands.add_parser("validate")
+    validate.add_argument("--manifest-kind", required=True)
+    validate.add_argument("--manifest-path", required=True)
+    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
+
+    if args.command == "select-bootstrap":
+        _write_selection(args.github_env, _CONTRACTS.resolve_bootstrap_registration(args.branch_name))
+        return 0
+    if args.command == "select-manual":
+        _write_selection(
+            args.github_env,
+            _CONTRACTS.resolve_manual_registration(args.github_ref, args.manifest_kind, args.manifest_path),
+        )
+        return 0
+    if args.command == "validate":
+        _CONTRACTS.validate_registration_selection(args.manifest_kind, args.manifest_path)
+        return 0
+
+    provider_run = _load_provider_run(args.provider_run_json)
+    envelope = _CONTRACTS.build_registration_envelope(args.manifest_path, args.commit_sha, provider_run)
+    _CONTRACTS.verify_github_receipt(envelope, provider_run)
+    args.output.write_text(json.dumps(envelope, sort_keys=True) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
+    return 0
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    raise SystemExit(main())

+def parse_utc_open_date(value: str) -> int:
+    """Parse one exact YYYY-MM-DD value as a UTC daily open in nanoseconds."""
+
+    if re.fullmatch(r"\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}", value) is None:
+        raise ValueError("open date must use exact YYYY-MM-DD format")
+    try:
+        parsed = datetime.strptime(value, "%Y-%m-%d").replace(tzinfo=UTC)
+    except ValueError as exc:
+        raise ValueError("open date must use exact YYYY-MM-DD format") from exc
+    return int(parsed.timestamp() * 1_000_000_000)
+
+
+def parse_timeframes(value: str) -> tuple[str, ...]:
+    """Parse one ordered, unique subset of supported kline timeframes."""
+
+    parts = tuple(part.strip() for part in value.split(","))
+    if not parts or any(not part for part in parts):
+        raise ValueError("timeframes must be a non-empty comma-separated list")
+    unsupported = tuple(part for part in parts if part not in SUPPORTED_TIMEFRAMES)
+    if unsupported:
+        raise ValueError(f"unsupported timeframes: {unsupported}")
+    if len(set(parts)) != len(parts):
+        raise ValueError("duplicate timeframes are not allowed")
+    return parts
+
